Compensate

/KOM-puhn-sayt/ - rhymes with wait · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Compensate means to pay someone for work, loss, or damage.

The ferry line compensated stranded passengers with a refund and meal vouchers before the night was out.

Worked Example

The movers cracked an heirloom mirror on the last flight of stairs. Nobody argued about whose hands slipped; the company's appraiser came Tuesday, valued the piece as the antique it was rather than the glass it had become, and a check for the full amount reached the family within two weeks.

Compensate is the exact word for what the company did, because compensate means to pay someone for work, loss, or damage — money set against the mirror's worth. Apologizing costs nothing and repairs nothing; reimburse would fit only if the family had first paid out cash of their own. Compensation weighs the loss and answers it with payment.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

reimburse: pays back money the person already laid out; compensation covers losses that never had receipts

remunerate: the formal word for paying someone for work done

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

shortchange: pay less than what is owed

underpay: keep the payment below the work's worth

Where it sits · how fully the loss is covered — console → compensate → indemnify

console vs. compensate: Console costs nothing — it soothes the person while the loss stays exactly where it fell.

indemnify vs. compensate: Indemnify goes further than compensate — compensation answers a loss after it lands; an indemnified party is shielded so the loss never lands on them at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: together, with

Root — pens

Root — pens: to weigh, to pay out (Latin pensare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to act

Put it together

Put it together: Com- (together) + pens (weigh) + -ate = to weigh one thing against another. Latin pensare is to weigh out; Roman pay was silver weighed on a scale, so compensating a loss is literally balancing the scale with payment.

Use the root in a new word: pension

Use the root in a new word: pension: A pension is pay weighed out on schedule — the same pens-, arriving every month after the working years end.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / business

Compensate is the word for making a loss good with payment — insurers, employers, courts. Reimburse is narrower and wants receipts; remunerate is stiffer and means wages. This unit's offset, met among the reference words, shares the balancing idea without the wallet: a gain can offset a loss even when nobody is paid.
